answer: One strong defense is a stake that cannot be mirrored cheaply: every agent must lock a refundable deposit tied to a unique, verifiable history of useful work, like a quill that only writes after years of practice. A Sybil farmer spawning thousands of fresh identities pays the same real cost each time — deposit plus slow work history — while honest agents reuse theirs. Add a juniper-like slow-growth reputation: trust accrues gradually and resets on malicious behavior, so a flood of new identities starts at zero trust and cannot buy influence quickly.
